title: Opening a Story: Time, Place & Background

sections.title: Framing a story before it starts moving
sections.content: A longer story needs a beginning that isn't an event yet — just the world the events will happen in. Hungarian opens this way with a time word, then a background description using *volt* ("was") and an adjective. *akkoriban* ("back then, in those days") and *korábban* ("earlier, previously") both go in the same front-of-sentence slot you already use for *tegnap* or *a következő nap* — before the subject, before everything else.

items.english: Back then, we lived in a small village.

items.spanish: Korábban egészen más volt a hangulat a városban.
items.english: Earlier, the mood in the town was completely different.

items.spanish: Régen nem volt itt semmi, csak mezők.
items.english: Long ago there was nothing here, just fields.

sections.content: Keep the background in plain past tense, same as everything else you already know — Hungarian doesn't switch to a separate "imperfect" verb form the way Spanish does. What signals "this is background, not the next event" is the time word up front (*akkoriban*, *korábban*) plus a describing verb like *volt*, not a different conjugation.
